text: The Patriots are heading into Buffalo with a defense significantly compromised by injury, as both Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore are ruled out for Sunday due to shoulder issues, while the offensive line took another hit with Greg Van Roten's placement on injured reserve due to a thigh injury—all of which compounds an already troubling reality for the 1-2 Patriots, who rank dead last in the NFL in offensive points per game at 9.7. Drake Maye addressed his right shoulder Wednesday and insists it's fine, instead pointing to poor decision-making as the culprit behind early struggles, while the offense is getting a boost with Matt Pryor joining the unit heading into a matchup against a Bills team led by Josh Allen, a quarterback remarkably skilled at moving past sloppy performances. On a lighter note, Mack Hollins was named the Week 4 NFLPA Community MVP after hosting a Special Olympics Family Field Day for over 125 athletes and their families, a reminder that there's still plenty of good work happening around a team that desperately needs to turn things around offensively.
